text_blocks.snippet: A mild cough, bloody sputum (coughing up blood), and weight loss are all potential symptoms of tuberculosis (TB). These symptoms, along with others like fever and night sweats, can indicate an active TB infection, which requires medical attention.

list.title: Tuberculosis (TB):
list.snippet: A contagious disease primarily affecting the lungs, though it can affect other parts of the body as well.

list.title: Active TB:
list.snippet: When latent TB infection progresses, it can lead to active disease with noticeable symptoms.

list.title: Bloody sputum (hemoptysis):
list.snippet: The discharge of blood or blood-stained mucus from the airways, which can be a symptom of TB, lung cancer, or other conditions.

list.title: Weight loss:
list.snippet: Unexplained weight loss can be a sign of various illnesses, including TB.

text_blocks.snippet: Important note: This information is for general knowledge and should not be taken as medical advice. If you are experiencing these symptoms, it is crucial to consult with a healthcare professional for proper diagnosis and treatment.
